I wrote these for the Humble Spring Sale and wanted to gather them into a single post for easy linking from the new Steam Group for covering all my reviews.

 

Beatbuddy
This is a game I wanted to like, but it just never really clicked with me. It's a rhythm game with nicely polished graphics, but the beat always seemed just slightly off to me. I don't know if it was just me, or if the response times were just odd on this game, but I normally don't have problems with this genre.

 

Capsized
I've only played this one for an hour or two, and while I'm not a huge fan of platforming shooters I think this one was better than usual. It had interesting weapons and a very different feel since you're in a low-gravity environment.

It isn't really sidescrolling either, the level I played was very complex and had a lot of verticality. For $0.99 it might be worth a look if you don't already have it from a bundle.

 

EvE
It's been a few expansions since I've played this MMO, but it really was a weird experience. You need to be interested in joining a social group (corporation) or you won't get far in this game - it has pretty heavy griefing and favors older players.

Leveling up is done over time, not by grinding - you just pick your skills and they train in so many hours, days, or weeks. So you can't be flying the biggest ships right off the bat, but if you want to pursue only that skill it won't take an absurd amount of time either. If you want every skill that will take a while though.

Combat and movement feel a bit more like playing a text adventure, but it has pretty visuals to keep you invested. You don't really steer, just set trajectories (circling the enemy) or waypoints and fire your guns when they come off cooldown. All the while you're watching your power levels, making sure your opponent doesn't warp away, etc.

It's a complex and unique experience, but emphasizes being a griefer if you enjoy that, and grouping up with others to protect yourself if you hate it.

 

Galactic Civilizations II
I haven't played this game in ages, but have fond memories of it. It's a 4x space RTS, probably the hardest one I've had the pleasure of playing. The enemy constantly has better technology than you, and only through sheer strategy will you be victorious.

That's a lot different than most games, and normally I would complain about it not being balanced, but it totally works for this game. I just started it up to see what resolutions it supports, and it works fine at 1080p, with no stretching to the interface or anything. The cutscenes are a bit fuzzy obviously, but that's to be expected.

So if you like a challenge, I'd highly recommend checking out this intense single-player RTS.

 

Guns of Icarus Online
I haven't played this one in a while, so some of the balance may have changed, since it is a multiplayer-only game and I think they're constantly tweaking it. Your experience is really going to depend on your crew. Each team picks out a flying ship, with people playing the role of gunner, engineer, and captain, trying to destroy the other team.

It isn't a free-for-all, there are usually a few ships on each side - and there are a number of different ship types too, each with different configurations and types of guns. One of the littlest ones has a flamethrower on the front, for instance.

When I was playing the ship types didn't feel completely balanced, but I think that may just be a matter of experience on how to kill your enemy. Each ship has a few hitboxes, for the ship itself and one for the balloon above - so you have to use strategy targeting different parts.

While the repairers are running around you may want to damage the engines so it can't move, and then your ship can sit out of range and pound them with impunity. Damaging the balloon makes it harder for them to stay aloft, and so on. It's a decent system that can be chaotic fun if your crew is good and your enemies are too, although sometimes it feels like it goes on a bit too long.

 

Hammerwatch
I gave this dungeon crawler a try a while ago, and just didn't find it very compelling (on top of the controls being a bit rough - you can only aim straight). This made it a bit slower than it should have been, but still wasn't particularly challenging. Cute pixel graphics, mediocre gameplay.

 

Lifeless Planet
I'll probably include this one in a Low Effort video at some point - it's sort of interesting, but is a walking simulator. There are some spots where you have to search around for a few items, but for the most part it's just walking and a little platforming.

The environment and story are better than I expected though, once you get past the initial barren platforming intro. So if you can get it cheap it might be worth a look - though I'm not sure most people will find it worth the $10 price tag from this sale.

 

Metal Dead
This point-and-click has a weird and wacky sense of humor, and it wasn't really my type of game. I also remember the resolution being pretty low, and obviously the graphics have a rough hand-drawn quality. Feels more flash game than polished release to me.

 

Monster Loves You
This is kind of a choose your own adventure game. There's a lot of text and you choose particular actions to perform as your monster grows into adulthood. This shapes how strong, brave, etc you are - and ultimately determines how the monsters interact with humans.

It was okay but not as engaging as I'd hoped - I liked watching Jesse Cox play it more than I enjoyed playing it myself. I just didn't feel that invested in my choices or monster.

There are multiple endings, so you can play it through a number of times - although you will run into the same answers if you repeat certain actions.

 

The Novelist
This is a weird game that I haven't played much of, it just didn't grab me. Basic premise is that you're a ghost that can inhabit light fixtures to avoid being caught. Your stealth move is to bounce from light to light to reach the room with your target.

You're basically stalking a family vacationing at your cabin, reading their diaries and trying to help them with their problems. So if you've always dreamed of being a light-jumping ghost therapist, then this is the game for you.

 

Orborun
This is one of those ball/runner type games where you're navigating through an aerial obstacle course, trying to get a fast time and pick up some collectibles.

Unfortunately, the controls weren't tight and responsive enough for my taste - and it didn't have the constant fast pace I'd look for in a game like this. Your guy will actually unfurl out of his ball form and lumber along if you slow down too much.

That might not have been a deal-breaker for me, but there just wasn't anything else to make it a particularly unique or exceptional game, which is why I ended up not reviewing it. It wasn't bad, but it didn't strike me as particularly great either.

 

Paranautical Activity
This is the only one for today that I haven't officially reviewed, and that's because I didn't enjoy the game. It's a first person dungeon crawler where you pick a class and are given a couple starting weapons.

This is the reason I never made it far - none of the weapon pairs feel particularly good. Some are inaccurate, others feel weak, and while this may have been more unique at the time it released to Early Access, I think there are at least a couple other games that fit this exact same genre now. So I'd give this a pass.

 

Particulars
This wasn't a bad game but the story wasn't particularly interesting to me, and the gameplay wasn't cohesive. Basically every single puzzle/minigame is different, so it feels pretty shallow - rather than letting you get invested and improve in one cool type of game.

 

Red Faction Collection
I've only played Red Faction 1 and Armageddon, but the whole series is really known for how destructible the environments are in the games. The first one is quite old and pretty innovative in that respect, you can tunnel through most of the rock in the game using your weapons.

Armageddon prevents terrain destruction but even massive buildings can be knocked down, and it's pretty cool to see - although the camera is a tight-third person view like console games. That makes it a bit more annoying than it should be.

The enemies in this game are pretty easy, and in many places you can just run past them until you hit one of the numerous cutscenes (which despawns everything chasing you). Weapons are also limited, 4 slots. It's very obviously a console experience, and has a lot of strange design decisions that seem more like they were focused on the technical aspects of the game instead of making sure it was fun.

 

Risk of Rain
The concept is solid but this game has a lot of technical issues, even if you aren't recording. If you are trying to record it's even worse since it doesn't play well with FRAPS or Dxtory (though I've heard that OBS sometimes works). It's a fun co-op experience, mowing down waves of monsters, grabbing loot and upgrades for your character - but the lag when the game gets busier can ruin this.

 

Sang Froid
I wanted to get into this game, because people I know have enjoyed it, but the tutorials are so long and wordy. The narrator droning on in his soothing voice almost put me to sleep. Maybe if it was interactive, rather than video-tutorial it would have been better.

That's a shame because the intro story seemed interesting, they just threw way too much non-game content at you in the beginning.

Three more that wouldn't fit in the OP because of wordcount:

 

Super Meat Boy

Everyone should know this game by now - but if you don't, it's a good hardcore precision platformer. The controls are tight and feel satisfying, and the levels are challenging but fair. If you hit a spike or spinning saw blade you get sent back to the start, and once you finally complete the level you can watch all your ghosts go at once, in a flood of bloody explosions. It's very cathartic.

 

Teslagrad

This cute puzzle platformer has an interesting story, though it's mostly told to you through context as well as the murals constructed from the collectibles throughout the game. These are sometimes quite difficult to reach - so you may not get all of them your first playthrough. Some of the boss fights can be tough, but it's an interesting little game if you like platformers.

 

Van Helsing

This one I haven't reviewed, and only played for an hour or two. It's a Diablo type experience, but felt really unbalanced to me. A lot of the enemies took far too long to die, even in areas where you're on the storyline quest - which should have a clear and proper balance. Maybe it gets better later in the game, but I wasn't willing to play it for several more hours to find out.
